newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks rebound to end higher, concern remains.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks rebound to end higher, concern remains.

text.p: Battered Thai stocks advanced 1.27 percent on Wednesday after falling for five straight trading days amid persistent concerns by foreigners over third quarter earnings and the slowing Thai economy, brokers said.

The SET index, which hit its intraday peak at 925.87, or up 20.53 points before the lunch break, closed 11.49 points higher to 916.83 on 4.8 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index rose 1.09 points higher to 68.74.
"The index rose sharply this morning on a technical rebound after falling heavily in the past few days. It fell in late afternoon on sales of bank and finance issues," said a broker.

The buying followed an improvement in market sentiment after medium-sized Bank of Ayudhya said earlier today that its unreviewed third quarter net profit rose to 1.57 billion baht, up from 1.18 billion baht the same period in 1995, brokers said.

"Investors thought after the Bank of Ayudhya announcement came out that earnings by larger banks during the third quarter might not be as bad as they had expected earlier," said Busaba Kunasirin of Chao Phya Finance and Securities.
Busaba said foreigners remained worried over third quarter earnings, the slowing of Thai economy and on a new government which is to be formed after a November 17 general election.
The banking sector was the only major sector on the board that fell today. It declined 0.05 percent. The transportation sector rose the most, gaining 3.64 percent.

Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, unchanged at 141 baht. Bank of Ayudhya was also unchanged at 80.50. National Finance and Securities rose 1.25 to 49 and Shinawatra Computer and Communications surged 16 to 398.
